column1: # Frozen ORACLE — issue #806. DO NOT REGENERATE. See the same warning in
# capacity-replay-corpus.tsv: these two files are ONE cut of one 48 h, and they
# move together or not at all. Re-cutting either alone leaves the differential
# comparing two unrelated windows while still passing every parse check.
# Every `event=all_exhausted` ENTER the running daemon logged over the SAME window
# as capacity-replay-corpus.tsv, from the SAME 48 h of wall-clock — but produced by
# a wholly different surface: the daemon's live tick decisions, written as it ran,
# versus an offline aggregate folded from the sample store. Two surfaces, two
# independent premises, one physical condition. That independence is the entire
# point: an aggregate fixture derived from the aggregator's own premise cannot
# refute the aggregator.
# Same redaction as the corpus: `hold` is the a1..a6 alias, `ts_off` is a signed
# offset from CORPUS_START.
# The daemon RE-ARMS its ENTER guard on any non-NoViableTarget tick, so these
# ENTERs over-count episodes by design. `count(ENTER) >= count(holds)` is therefore
# NOT an invariant in either direction and is NEVER gated on — the ratio is only
# ever reported as a diagnostic. What IS asserted is DETECTION and CAUSE COVERAGE:
# over a window the daemon spent cornered, the aggregate must see a hold AT ALL
# rather than print UNKNOWN, and must name BOTH of the causes the oracle names.
# Per-ENTER containment — "at each instant below there is a hold covering it" — is
# deliberately NOT asserted: these rows are ENTER EDGES, not episode spans, so the
# oracle carries no span to contain, and a coverage gap around any single edge
# would fail a containment gate for a reason that says nothing about the metric.
# Columns, tab-separated:  ts_off  hold  cause
